steps.reason: Before inspecting or changing the machine, choose whether ThisCodex should attempt recoverable setup steps itself or explain every step for manual execution.

on_fail.next_command: rerun `thiscodex init` and choose auto or manual as the first answer; non-interactive automation may pass --automation-mode auto

steps.reason: First we check the operating system and installed tools so the installer can explain only the steps that apply to this machine.
Skill placement only copies SKILL.md; guided onboarding configures a usable bot workspace.

on_fail.next_command: rerun `thiscodex init` for interactive guided recovery (an AI agent: relay this choice to the user — do NOT self-answer); non-interactive opt-out only: thiscodex init --apply --yes --answers <answers.json>; or abort

steps.reason: ThisCodex runs a Codex bot daemon. On Windows, WSL gives the bot a Linux shell, tmux, and predictable paths.
ThisCodex must know the repository root so generated aliases can return to the repo you chose, not a fixed developer path.
Guided onboarding needs the workspace or vault root before it can draft bot instructions.
ThisCodex needs one stable bot working directory for AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, thread id, and runner files.
Choose the short runtime name used for the tmux session, BOT_NAME, and one-word shell aliases. This prevents a custom bot from silently launching as the generic 'thiscodex' session.

Connecting an Obsidian wiki (vault) path lets this bot save chat-directed Markdown output there. This is a first-class but OPTIONAL question: leaving it blank never blocks bot creation, and the completion notice explains how to start from a sample vault and connect later.
Discord token and bridge state live outside the repo and outside BOT_WD, so safe-mode Codex cannot silently self-upgrade privileges.
Codex loads skills from ordered scan layers. User layer is shared across repos; repo layer is isolated to this checkout.
.codex-plugin marketplace metadata is a secondary discovery path. The primary install still uses Codex skill scan directories.
Codex app-server can clamp per-turn sandbox requests unless ~/.codex/config.toml allows the requested ceiling.

When browser tools are required, automatic mode installs Playwright CLI and MCP, registers the MCP with Codex, re-detects the registration, and proves direct use with a headless DOM-click E2E before onboarding can continue.
Danger-full-access is powerful. This step is opt-in only, backs up config.toml, and exists for trusted hosts running unattended Codex bots.
tmux keeps the infra window and Codex TUI attached to the same bot session. Without it, the daemon guide cannot start cleanly.

on_fail.next_command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

steps.reason: Guided onboarding materializes runner files (run.sh, infra-launch.sh, progress config) in the bot working directory so the bot can be launched without memorizing commands.

Recommended by default: one-word start/restart and stop helpers call the runner generated from confirmed paths; only an explicit no skips them. The alias block is printed for you to paste, so nothing edits your rc file automatically.

Aliases are generated only after repo and BOT_WD are confirmed. Start cleans up only the exact same-named tmux session before relaunch, stop targets that exact session, and no developer-machine path is baked in.

Choose how often this bot should proactively report progress: per_task means meaningful subtask or milestone completion, 1/3/5 minutes configures bridge heartbeat, off disables bridge heartbeat, custom requires operator follow-up.
The runner files make the safe launch command repeatable without auto-starting a daemon.

steps.when: answers.automation_mode == 'auto' and mode == 'doctor' or answers.automation_mode == 'auto' and mode == 'smoke'
